title: Choose the visual world for VED.EXE
question: The roll assigned The Patent Filing. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Patent Filing
options.lineage: utility patent specifications: cover sheet, drawing sheets, numbered claims
options.thesis: Every project is filed as an invention: a figure with numbered callouts and claims that state exactly what the engineering does.
materials: two-column spec with gutter line numbers
options.viewport: Cover sheet: bibliographic block (Title, Inventor Ved S. Chauhan, Assignee SNOWBROS, Abstract) left; FIG. 1 right, an exploded axonometric stack of real project screenshots with numbered callouts you hover to lift and click to open.
options.risk: Can tip into costume if the codes and FIG labels are decorative rather than navigational; the wit must stay dry and every claim true.

raised.raise: Attention is the light: the hovered callout and its plate take the single cobalt ink, everything else stays graphite.
One strict gutter rules every sheet, with line numbers in the margin, the way a spec body is set.
Figures draw themselves once as they enter, a single timed emergence, then hold still.
Type scale is mapped to importance of the claim, never to decoration.

options.label: The Component Datasheet
options.lineage: semiconductor datasheets: pinouts, electrical characteristics, revision history
options.thesis: Each project is a part you could drop into a system: pinout for architecture, characteristics table for real numbers, revision history for releases.
options.viewport: Page 1 of a datasheet: part number VED.EXE, features list, a pinout of the stack, ordering information as contact.
options.risk: Familiar to hardware engineers but dense; risks reading as a table-heavy PDF if the curves and diagrams are not generous.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight Bay
options.thesis: Projects develop into view station by station.
options.viewport: A developer tray where a screenshot emerges from gray.
options.case: Fuses loosely: the reveal suits screenshots but engineers do not identify with photo chemistry, and amber hurts reading.
options.kept: One timed emergence per figure instead of scattered reveals.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Time reads upward on a bilateral staff.
options.viewport: A center staff with build activity as notation.
options.case: Fuses poorly: elegant for the activity graph, opaque for case studies.
options.kept: A single strict layout law, the gutter, that every sheet obeys.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.viewport: A dark field where projects bloom near the pointer.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the neon-on-black rut the brief bans, and it hides content.
options.risk: Particles and glow the brief explicitly rules out.
options.kept: Pointer attention as the only illumination.

options.label: Variety Telop Captions
options.thesis: Captions sized to the emotion of the moment.
options.viewport: Project names landing as tilted outlined captions.
options.case: Fuses poorly: loud where the brief asks for restraint.

options.label: Suminagashi Ink Basin
options.thesis: The page as a liquid surface you stir.
options.viewport: A basin where each drop is a project.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a heavy WebGL scene the brief warns against, no product clarity.

options.label: Rain Night Cityscape
options.thesis: Work as lights across a city at night.
options.viewport: A skyline where windows are repos.
options.case: Fuses poorly: atmospheric, but projects become anonymous windows.
options.kept: One live state layer (build activity) as the only thing that changes with time.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A premium dark developer portfolio, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role left, featured project right, sections below in the order visitors expect.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other strong dev portfolios by design.
